jobs.title: Founding Growth & Creator Partnerships
jobs.mission: Build the first repeatable path from learner acquisition to speaking, payment, and creator supply.
responsibilities: Define the first anchor learner cohort and validate the funnel from outreach and acquisition through first speech, repeat use, and payment.
Design and run channel and message experiments, connecting CAC, activation, paid conversion, and retention in every decision.
Source education, language, and content creators and own personalized outreach, meetings, commercial terms, contracts, and pilot operations.
Build and operate the pipeline from creator outreach to repeatable supply and learner selection or purchase.
Turn customer rejection, churn, and language into decision-ready evidence for weekly reviews with the founder.
Maintain source, usage-right, compensation, and contract records and escalate rights or trust risks immediately.
requirements: Evidence that you personally delivered acquisition, conversion, or partnership outcomes for an app, subscription service, advertising program, or creator campaign.
Ability to contact unfamiliar customers or creators directly and change the target, message, or offer based on rejection evidence.
Ability to manage acquisition, first value, payment, and repeat use as one funnel rather than optimizing impressions or installs.
Ability to define the next experiment and stopping criteria with a small budget and incomplete data.
Ability to negotiate partner terms while protecting long-term trust.
preferred: Hands-on performance or growth marketing experience for an app or subscription product.
Acquisition, CRM, or lifecycle experience in edtech or consumer subscriptions.
Creator sourcing, outreach, negotiation, and campaign ownership in influencer marketing or an MCN.
Experience measuring paid or creator channels through payment and retention.
Experience building in an early-stage team and stopping failed hypotheses with evidence.

jobs.title: Founding Conversation Learning Scientist
jobs.employmentType: Paid project with subsequent hiring review
jobs.mission: Design training and assessment that help Korean speakers construct and sustain English conversations appropriate to their purpose and audience.
responsibilities: Design a conversation capability model linking conventions, functions, purpose, empathy, and utterance-generation difficulty.
Build progression from shadowing through recall, variation, personal experience, persuasion, and unexpected questions.
Observe Korean learners' speech and classify failures in retrieval, discourse, fluency, interaction, and anxiety.
Develop rubrics, assessment tasks, and before-and-after comparisons to measure transfer.
Review AI conversation tasks and feedback for linguistic validity, educational benefit, and misjudgment risk.
Translate learner research and experiments into product requirements with the founder, product, and engineering teams.
End ineffective hypotheses based on evidence and design the next curriculum and product experiments.
requirements: Applied experience in applied linguistics, second-language acquisition, English education, or learning science.
Ability to observe Korean learners' speech errors and diagnose their causes systematically.
Experience designing and improving task-based training, curricula, or speaking-assessment rubrics.
Ability to turn interviews and speech evidence into education or product decisions.
Ability to make hypotheses measurable independently of English fluency.
Ability to independently evaluate the linguistic validity and learning effects of AI output.
preferred: English conversation teaching, research, or curriculum experience with Korean adults.
Experience developing edtech, speaking training, or consumer learning products.
Familiarity with CEFR, ACTFL, and performance-based speaking assessment.
Experience combining learning experiments, qualitative research, and basic statistics.
Experience evaluating AI tutors, LLM feedback, or speech assessment.
Experience connecting research rapidly to prototypes and decisions in an early-stage team.

jobs.title: English Speaking Content Contributor
jobs.mission: Resolve the initial content cold start by writing and validating small units of words, idioms, phrasal verbs, and speaking situations used in real conversations.
responsibilities: Choose a published word, idiom, phrasal verb, or conversation mission and submit it.
Write core meanings, real usage situations, original English examples, and natural Korean explanations.
Record a short follow-up response, difficulty, and register.
AI may assist drafting, but personally verify meaning, sentence patterns, naturalness, and references.
Provide one revision within the stated deadline when requested by a reviewer.
Accepted items are assembled into vocabulary, idiom, phrasal-verb, rehearsal, and home-feed training content.
requirements: Ability to write concise, accurate Korean and English explanations and examples.
Write original examples instead of copying textbooks, dictionaries, subtitles, or blogs.
Record references and reasoning in the required format.
Follow acceptance, copyright, and content-safety standards.
Agree to voluntary short-term mission participation without required working hours or ongoing participation.
preferred: Study in English literature, English education, translation, applied linguistics, or TESOL.
Translation, proofreading, teaching, textbook, or dialogue-writing experience.
Experience explaining common English errors made by Korean learners.
Experience using or creating rehearsal, shadowing, or conversation materials.
jobs.compensation: KRW 1,000 per accepted item; up to 20 items and KRW 20,000 per contributor.

jobs.title: Conversation Content Producer (PD)
jobs.mission: Develop an English conversation format suited to its performers and connect a four-to-six-episode pilot to Naepopquiz training, reuse, and purchases.
responsibilities: Define the learners, repeatable program format, four-to-six-episode plan, and production schedule.
Discover and recruit performers, coordinating episode participation terms and schedules.
Deliver scripts, filming, editing, titles, thumbnails, and short-form assets personally or through agreed collaborators.
Coordinate educational review of expressions, translations, and difficulty, and provide training-pack source materials.
Record sources, music and video rights, performers' name, image, and voice permissions, and advertising disclosures per episode.
Apply traceable CTAs and campaign or deep-link identifiers to measure app entry and learning after viewing.
Recommend retaining, revising, or ending the format and evaluate season contracts or shared-IP arrangements.
requirements: A portfolio of digital video projects completed from planning through publication.
Ability to turn performers' strengths into repeatable interview, entertainment, or education formats.
Ability to manage casting, filming, editing, schedules, and quality with a small budget.
Ability to interpret app entry, training starts and completion, and purchases rather than views alone.
Ability to record copyright, personality rights, advertising disclosures, and agreed usage scope.
Ability to independently deliver agreed outcomes and deadlines rather than working-hour commitments.
preferred: Pilot or season production for web entertainment, interviews, education, or creator-led shows.
Direct discovery and recruitment of emerging performers, experts, or education creators.
Repurposing footage into full episodes, Shorts, Reels, and educational content.
Edtech, English conversation, shadowing, or learning-content production.
Branded content, sponsorship, or creator revenue-share experience.
Analysis of post-viewing behavior with GA4, Firebase Analytics, or YouTube Analytics.
